image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Enclosed noodle soup cart with a stainless broth well, hanging ladles and a glazed side panel Materials: dented stainless steel, steam-clouded acrylic, worn painted panels.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,800/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/8 unique geometries, two grime canvases. Turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement, covering ONLY what is genuinely open -- the two handle loops, the wheels between rim and hub, and a thin arc of the basin inner wall -- painted with holeviz to confirm the panel is no longer classified at any azimuth.

featureReviews.evidence: Built 1.520 x 1.508 x 0.884 m against a declared 1.50 x 1.50 x 0.88 (depth corrected from 0.75 on the proxy's 0.871). Every station is the proxy band table's, read in metres at the declared height: near-cubic cabinet 1.06 x 0.945 x 0.76 from 0.20 to 1.145, counter 1.096 x 0.796 x 0.060 on top of it, horizontal U handles at y 1.090 out to +-0.745, r 0.175 open wheels at x -0.455 and z +-0.405, casters at x +0.462, the ladle alone above 1.205.
featureReviews.notes: The previous build read the same proxy as a cabinet 0.30-0.98 by 0.66 deep on r 0.27 wheels -- a squat long box under two giant discs.

featureReviews.evidence: An OVAL basin 0.864 x 0.640 at the rim, 79% of the counter's length and 91% of its depth, solved from the rim ellipse's screen extents on the plate against the counter's projected plan vectors; a lathe revolved at the depth radius and stretched 1.35 in x. Floor at 1.026, broth at 1.116 (97 mm below the lip), a rolled rim that tucks back under the counter top, a ladle bowl half out of the broth with its handle to 1.500. The counter is two stacked pierced plates for its bullnose, with a pressed groove and three scoring lines.
featureReviews.notes: Three defects fixed here in turn: the body box's own top face cut across the inside of the bowl and rendered as a flat dark disc; a rim that folded back under itself was corner-split into a gear; and a shell that stopped at its lip showed its own backside as a dark ring.

featureReviews.evidence: Four elevations as extrusions with a real opening cut in each, 15 mm proud of the dark body on 0.075 stiles; two doors -- a light leaf on the +X half of the long face with a moulding, a pull and two strap hinges, and a dark one filling the -X end; two OPEN bicycle wheels of a tyre ring, a rim ring, twelve prism spokes, a hub and a chrome dome cap, instanced and each a named pivot; two swivel casters with a top plate, a fork and a rubber wheel; U handles with ferrules. Wear as a rust hem, a narrow creep at each panel reveal, blooms at the bottom corners and a bleed under each hinge.
featureReviews.notes: A broad stain across each stile was tried first and read as tan camouflage.
